question: A medico-legal radiographic age estimation report that states 'estimated age: 17 years' (a single figure) is more useful than one stating 'estimated age: 16–18 years' (a range), because it gives the court a definitive answer.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is false. Radiographic age estimation has inherent biological variability that makes a single precise age dishonest. Reporting a RANGE (e.g., '16–18 years') is the medico-legally and scientifically correct approach. The court applies the standard of proof to determine whether the person was a minor; it needs an honest range, not fabricated precision.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct — this statement is false. A single figure overstates the precision of skeletal age estimation and is scientifically indefensible. The court requires an HONEST estimate with its uncertainty range. Reporting a range such as '16–18 years' is the only defensible approach; it allows the court to apply the appropriate legal standard of proof rather than rely on false precision.
